owner: verapdf syntax; custom engine semantic extraction
requirement: Read permitted XMP encodings into the same semantic field value before checking EA-PDF meaning. Do not compare incidental XML nesting or prefixes for namespaces where EA-PDF does not mandate the prefix. The three EA-PDF prefixes remain explicitly constrained by Table 14.
permitted_forms: Unqualified normal simple values as element text or rdf:Description property attributes.
Structure values with nested rdf:Description or rdf:parseType="Resource".
All-simple structure fields as attributes under the applicable XMP shorthand constraints.
Qualified values with rdf:value and qualifier fields, including permitted typed inner-node interpretation.
URI-valued fields via rdf:resource; normal strings remain distinct from URI-valued data.
Top-level properties split among equivalent rdf:Description nodes with a consistent resource.
prohibited_general_rdf_forms: Top-level typed nodes in place of rdf:Description.
rdf:parseType="Literal" or general forms outside the XMP subset.
Array rdf:Description plus rdf:type replacing rdf:Bag/rdf:Seq/rdf:Alt.
rdf:_n replacing required rdf:li array members.
test_contract: Equivalent valid XMP fields must give identical EA-PDF results; generic syntax failures must be attributed to upstream validation, not invented EA-PDF requirements.
status: V03 implements tested simple attributes, nested Description/parseType structures, qualified rdf:value forms, typed inner agent access, URI/string distinction and top-level description scoping. This is semantic extraction, not a complete generic XMP syntax validator.

requirement: Preserve array kind and member order. To/From/Cc/Bcc use ordered FOAF-agent arrays; assets, email containers and attachments are unordered record sets. In-Reply-To is described as unordered despite the printed word sequence; retain this terminology question explicitly. A scalar or wrong-kind container must not become valid merely because it flattens to the same strings.
status: V03 checks supplied email/assets/attachments as unordered structured record arrays and To/From/Cc/Bcc as ordered structured agent arrays, preserving order in comparisons. Attachment absence versus empty set and In-Reply-To terminology remain explicit expert questions.

requirement: Each listed address is a structured agent with the required FOAF mailbox property. Optional name and additional FOAF fields remain allowed. Equivalent permitted XMP typed/qualified forms must be interpreted correctly. Match the full FOAF namespace, not local tag names alone. Do not invent SMTP lexical restrictions from the current source parser.
status: Meaning reviewed; exact mailbox literal/URI representation and malformed source normalization remain explicit expert questions.

requirement: Each represented email requires a unique Mail_GUID as an XMP normal (non-URI) simple string. No canonical UUID lexical form is required. Compare its Unicode value exactly; do not trim, case-fold, normalize Unicode or reinterpret a URI-looking GUID as an RDF URI.
test_contract: URI-looking normal GUID strings remain normal text; differently cased or whitespace-different GUIDs must not merge. Required-field and duplicate checks are separate from canonical UUID formatting.
status: Implemented in V03: exact normal-string extraction, required canonical property name, uniqueness and XMP/DPM/structure/attachment-owner joins; authored regression and frozen corpus evidence tracked separately.

owner: custom field applicability and expected types; generic serialization upstream
requirement: Keep Table 18 Sent xsd:dateTime, standard xmp:CreateDate XMP Date, Table 12 Mail_Sent PDF date string, and embedded Params ModDate PDF date distinct. The partial precision legal for XMP Date does not automatically satisfy xsd:dateTime. Do not equate all date fields or infer provenance from matching dates.
status: Type distinctions reviewed; exact edition-specific lexical details and boundary fixtures remain to be checked.

requirement: XMP source Checksum and attachment CheckSum are 32 hexadecimal ASCII characters; PDF Params CheckSum is 16 raw MD5 bytes. Checksum letter case is insignificant, GUID case is significant. Sizes describe uncompressed stored streams except where Table 18 explicitly describes original encoded message bytes. PDF and XMP filenames need not be identical when sanitization is necessary.
status: Requirement reviewed; mandatory schema and recommended presence remain separate.
